english: Nine distinct books, namely three volumes of an encyclopaedia, three novels and three dictionaries, are arranged in a row on a shelf. The three volumes of the encyclopaedia are to be next to one another (in any order), no two novels are to be adjacent, and no novel is to be adjacent to a volume of the encyclopaedia. Then the number of such arrangements is ______.
hindi: नौ भिन्न पुस्तकें, अर्थात् एक विश्वकोश के तीन खण्ड, तीन उपन्यास तथा तीन शब्दकोश, एक शेल्फ पर एक पंक्ति में रखी जाती हैं। विश्वकोश के तीनों खण्ड एक-दूसरे के साथ (किसी भी क्रम में) रखने हैं, कोई दो उपन्यास आसन्न नहीं होने चाहिए, तथा कोई उपन्यास विश्वकोश के किसी खण्ड के आसन्न नहीं होना चाहिए। तब ऐसी व्यवस्थाओं की संख्या ______ है।
solution: Bundle the volumes: block $B$ ($3!$ inner orders) with 3 dictionaries $\Rightarrow$ 4 units, $4!$ orders
Novels go into the 5 gaps of these 4 units, at most one per gap (no two novels adjacent)
The two gaps next to $B$ are forbidden, wherever $B$ is (at an end, one of them is the end gap) $\Rightarrow$ 3 gaps left
solution_full: Bundle method: since the three volumes are together, treat them as one block $B$, which can be ordered internally in $3!=6$ ways.
Arrange $B$ and the three dictionaries: 4 units in a row, $4!=24$ orders.
Gap method: the novels are placed in the 5 gaps (two ends and three between units). No two novels are adjacent exactly when each gap receives at most one novel.

A novel is adjacent to a volume exactly when it is in one of the two gaps on either side of $B$. If $B$ is in the middle, these are two inner gaps; if $B$ is at an end, they are the end gap and the gap after $B$. In every case exactly 2 gaps are forbidden and 3 remain.
The three distinct novels must occupy the three allowed gaps, one in each: $3!=6$ ways. Each such novel is then flanked only by dictionaries or the shelf end.
originality_note: New: the bundle and gap methods combined so that the bundle removes exactly two gaps wherever it stands (the end case looks different but is not), which decides that the novels fill the remaining gaps exactly (way 4: an invariant hidden behind a case split). Closest known: 'books of the same subject together' and 'no two girls together'. Different because: the forbidden gaps depend on the bundle, and the first design with two dictionaries gave 0 (checked by brute force) and was enlarged.
blueprint_concepts: Arrangements with specified objects together (bundle method)
Arrangements with specified objects separated (gap method)

concept_use.Arrangements with specified objects toge: The three volumes are treated as one block with 3! internal orders.
concept_use.Arrangements with specified objects sepa: The novels are placed in the gaps between the four units, with the two gaps beside the block excluded.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed by an independent brute-force enumeration in Python (sympy/itertools), is unique and matches the Answer Plan. Checked by enumerating all 9! orders (864), that the end-of-shelf case also forbids two gaps, and that 864 is a positive 3-digit integer as planned. Changed: the first draft with two dictionaries had answer 0, so a third dictionary was added.
key_step: Seeing that the encyclopaedia block always kills exactly two gaps, leaving three gaps for three novels.
justification: Bundle and gap methods linked, with an apparent case split (block at an end or inside) that resolves to one count. Two ideas, numerical answer; level 3.
